instruments.notes: WTI-based 2000 hedge; instrument name not visible in text (preceding sentence truncated). Above $28.43 monthly avg WTI Company pays counterparty the excess; at or below $22.00 counterparty pays Company $2.00 per barrel (flat payment, not a standard floor).
instruments.evidence_quote:
average WTI exceeds $28.43 per barrel, the Company will pay the counterparty the
difference  between  the  average WTI and $28.43, and to the extent WTI is at or
below  $22.00,  the  counterparty  will  pay  the Company $2.00 per barrel.

instruments.notes: WTI call options purchased in 1995 in anticipation of the forward oil sale; strike is weighted average $20.42 (stored in ceiling_price field as the call strike). Volumes and expirations coincide with forward oil sale deliveries, which complete March 2000; volume not stated. Fair value change recorded as gain of $6.1 million in 1999 (6,150 thousand in other income table). Offset by sold calls in Nov 1999.
instruments.evidence_quote:
purchased  WTI  benchmark call options to retain the ability to benefit from WTI
price  increases  above  a  weighted  average  price  of $20.42 per barrel.

instruments.notes: In November 1999 Company sold WTI call options with same notional quantities, strike and contract period as the remaining purchased calls, for a premium of $4.4 million, eliminating exposure to future value changes. Strike $20.42 inferred only as 'same strike price' as the purchased calls; volume not stated.
instruments.evidence_quote:
the Company sold WTI benchmark call options
with  the  same  notional  quantities,  strike  price and contract period as the
remaining  call  option  contracts outstanding for a premium of $4.4 million

hedging_summary.stated_hedging_policy: From time to time uses financial market transactions including swaps, collars and options with creditworthy counterparties to reduce pricing risk on a portion of oil and gas sold; no trading purposes.
